```{r setup-correlations, include=FALSE}
library(here)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7, dpi = 110)
# ---- PCA.R ----------------------------------------
# =============================================================================
# PCA.R
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A principal component analysis per block of the survey (sections/pca.Rmd),
# complementing the within-block correlation matrices (sections/correlations.Rmd).
# The correlation screen shows which PAIRS of items are near-duplicates; this
# shows whether a block has a STRUCTURE, decomposing the same Spearman matrix.
#
# Components are estimated within one block at a time, so C1 of one block has
# nothing to do with C1 of another. pca_block() computes one block and returns
# the numbers; the section renders them.
# =============================================================================

# psych is called through its namespace rather than attached: it masks several
# common names.

# ---- Editable decisions --------------------------------------------------------
METHOD        <- "spearman"  # the matrix the correlation screen plots
ROTATION      <- "oblimin"   # oblique: sub-scales are expected to correlate
LOAD_MIN      <- 0.40        # minimum |loading| to call an item a member
MIN_ITEMS_PCA <- 5           # below this: reduced report, no rotation
MODAL_MAX     <- 0.95        # flag an item if one answer holds this share
N_ITER_PA     <- 100         # parallel-analysis iterations
TEXT_CAP      <- 46          # characters of wording on an axis
SEED          <- 2026        # parallel analysis simulates data; fix its seed

# Override the retention rule for a named block, e.g. c(Beliefs = 3). The
# empirical rule (parallel analysis) applies to every block not named here.
FORCE_K <- c()


# ---- The blocks ------------------------------------------------------------------
# In survey order; BLOCK_NAMES also names the matrices in sections/correlations.Rmd.
# Beliefs and Behaviour use the reverse-scored copies, so that high means more
# pro-liberalisation on every item and a loading's sign is not a wording artefact.
BLOCK_NAMES <- c("Beliefs", "Behaviour", "Substance use",
                 "Policy preference", "Involvement")
BLOCKS <- setNames(
  list(
    scored_copies(select_items("beliefs", names(pilot))),
    scored_copies(select_items("gedrag_beleid", names(pilot))),
    subst_cols,                       # own use per substance group (four items)
    unname(POLICY_COLUMNS),
    select_items("betrokkenheid", names(pilot))
  ),
  BLOCK_NAMES
)
BLOCKS <- lapply(BLOCKS, intersect, ANALYSIS_COLUMNS)
stopifnot(all(unlist(BLOCKS) %in% names(pilot)))

# a component needs at least a pair of items
BLOCKS_FITTED <- Filter(function(cols) length(cols) >= 2L, BLOCKS)
stopifnot(length(BLOCKS_FITTED) > 0)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# pca_block()
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One block: decide how many components it supports, fit them, and return the
# numbers. It prints nothing and writes nothing.
#
# set.seed() lives here rather than around the loop: parallel analysis
# simulates data, so a block's retention count must not depend on how many
# blocks happened to be fitted before it.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
pca_block <- function(cols, block_name, pilot) {
  set.seed(SEED)
  x <- as.matrix(pilot[cols])

  # An item with NO variance at all has no correlations either: its row and
  # column of R come back NA, and eigen() then refuses the entire matrix rather
  # than just that item. Such an item cannot load on any component, so it is
  # dropped here instead of taking the whole block down with it.
  #
  # This is the extreme end of the near-constant problem handled further down:
  # items that do vary, however slightly, are kept and reported via modal_share.
  constant <- vapply(seq_len(ncol(x)), function(j) {
    v <- x[, j][!is.na(x[, j])]
    length(v) == 0L || stats::var(v) == 0
  }, logical(1))
  if (any(constant)) {
    message(sprintf("%s: dropped %d item(s) with no variance in this sample: %s",
                    block_name, sum(constant), paste(cols[constant], collapse = ", ")))
    x    <- x[, !constant, drop = FALSE]
    cols <- cols[!constant]
  }

  k_items <- ncol(x)

  # The correlation matrix, from the SAME call the correlation screen makes -
  # not a re-derivation. Everything downstream (principal, KMO, Bartlett) reads
  # a correlation matrix, so this is the only place the data enter the model.
  R <- cor(x, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = METHOD)

  # Parallel analysis is the exception: it needs raw data, not a matrix, and
  # psych::fa.parallel() has no method = "spearman". Spearman IS Pearson on the
  # ranks, so ranking first gives it the same matrix rather than silently
  # switching the whole retention decision to Pearson. na.last = "keep"
  # matters: rank()'s default would hand the "Geen mening" cells a real rank.
  complete <- complete.cases(x)
  ranked   <- apply(x[complete, , drop = FALSE], 2, rank, na.last = "keep")

  n_obs  <- sum(complete)
  eig    <- eigen(R, only.values = TRUE)$values
  var_pc <- eig / k_items * 100          # % of total variance per component

  # Near-constant items. The report's Analyses tab lists near-zero variance as
  # one of the things that biases a network, and it breaks a PCA for the same
  # reason: an item almost everyone answers identically has nothing left to
  # covary with, so it cannot load anywhere and it drags the block's KMO down.
  # It is also what makes fa.parallel's resampling warn about a zero standard
  # deviation - a resample can easily draw only the modal answer - which is why
  # that call is wrapped below rather than left to emit dozens of warnings.
  modal_share <- apply(x, 2, function(v) {
    v <- v[!is.na(v)]
    max(table(v)) / length(v)
  })

  # ---- how many components? --------------------------------------------------
  # Thin blocks are not asked the question at all: with 3 or 4 items there is
  # not enough covariance structure for a second component to mean anything,
  # and rotation is undefined for a single component.
  thin <- k_items < MIN_ITEMS_PCA
  if (thin) {
    k_pa <- NA_integer_
    k    <- 1L
  } else {
    # fa.parallel() cat()s its own one-line verdict even with plot = FALSE;
    # swallowed here so the caller is the single reporter of it.
    invisible(capture.output(suppressWarnings(
      pa <- psych::fa.parallel(ranked, fa = "pc", n.iter = N_ITER_PA,
                               plot = FALSE)
    )))
    k_pa <- pa$ncomp
    # never extract more components than the block can support
    k <- max(1L, min(as.integer(k_pa), k_items - 1L))
  }
  if (block_name %in% names(FORCE_K)) k <- as.integer(FORCE_K[[block_name]])

  # ---- fit -------------------------------------------------------------------
  rotation <- if (k == 1) "none" else ROTATION
  fit <- psych::principal(R, nfactors = k, rotate = rotation, n.obs = n_obs)

  loads <- unclass(fit$loadings)
  colnames(loads) <- paste0("C", seq_len(ncol(loads)))
  primary   <- apply(abs(loads), 1, which.max)
  prim_load <- apply(abs(loads), 1, max)
  assigned  <- prim_load >= LOAD_MIN

  # `wording` is keyed by the RAW variable name, so the _scored suffix has to
  # come off before the lookup - reverse-scoring does not change the question.
  text_full <- sub("^.*? - ", "",
                   gsub("[\r\n]+", " ", wording[sub("_scored$", "", cols)]))
  text_full[is.na(text_full)] <- cols[is.na(text_full)]

  # Two shapes of the same result. The WIDE table is what reads well in a
  # console and in a knitr::kable(), one row per item; but its columns depend
  # on how many components that block retained, so blocks cannot be stacked in
  # that shape. The csv is therefore built LONG, which stacks cleanly and is
  # what any downstream filtering or joining wants anyway.
  wide <- data.frame(
    block     = block_name,
    number    = seq_along(cols),
    variable  = cols,
    wording   = text_full,
    round(as.data.frame(loads), 3),
    primary   = ifelse(assigned, paste0("C", primary), "-"),
    prim_load = round(prim_load, 3),
    row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE
  )

  long <- data.frame(
    block     = block_name,
    number    = rep(seq_along(cols), times = ncol(loads)),
    variable  = rep(cols, times = ncol(loads)),
    wording   = rep(text_full, times = ncol(loads)),
    component = rep(colnames(loads), each = length(cols)),
    loading   = round(as.vector(loads), 3),
    primary   = rep(ifelse(assigned, paste0("C", primary), "-"),
                    times = ncol(loads)),
    prim_load = rep(round(prim_load, 3), times = ncol(loads)),
    row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # Reliability of each retained component, on the items assigned to it. Alpha
  # only: omega on a handful of items at this n is not stable enough to report.
  # suppressMessages as well as suppressWarnings - on the 0-100 sliders alpha()
  # advises increasing the number of categories, which is about its frequency
  # table, not about the coefficient being reported.
  alphas <- vapply(seq_len(k), function(ci) {
    members <- cols[assigned & primary == ci]
    if (thin || length(members) < 3) return(NA_real_)
    a <- suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
      psych::alpha(pilot[complete, members], warnings = FALSE)))
    a$total$raw_alpha
  }, numeric(1))
  n_members <- vapply(seq_len(k),
                      function(ci) sum(assigned & primary == ci), integer(1))

  # ---- figures ---------------------------------------------------------------
  # Scree: observed eigenvalues against the flat "one component per item" line.
  scree_df <- data.frame(component = seq_along(eig), eigenvalue = eig)
  scree <- ggplot(scree_df, aes(x = component, y = eigenvalue)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
    geom_line(colour = "grey30") +
    geom_point(size = 1.8,
               colour = ifelse(scree_df$component <= k, "#B2182B", "grey45")) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(eig)) +
    labs(title = paste0(block_name, ": scree"), x = "component",
         y = "eigenvalue") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

  # Loading heatmap, in the same visual grammar as the correlation matrices:
  # item wording down the rows, the same blue-white-red diverging scale on a
  # fixed [-1, 1], and a black outline on the cells that clear the membership
  # threshold. Read side by side, a strongly correlated pair in the matrix
  # should be a pair of cells in the same column here.
  tiles <- expand.grid(variable = cols, component = colnames(loads),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  tiles$loading <- as.vector(loads)
  tiles$flag    <- abs(tiles$loading) >= LOAD_MIN
  # Wrapped on the axis below rather than truncated here: several items share
  # an opening clause, and a cut-off label makes them indistinguishable.
  row_labels    <- paste0(seq_along(cols), ". ", text_full)
  tiles$row_lab <- factor(row_labels[match(tiles$variable, cols)],
                          levels = row_labels)

  loadings_plot <- ggplot(tiles, aes(x = component, y = row_lab,
                                     fill = loading)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_tile(data = tiles[tiles$flag, ], colour = "black", fill = NA) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.2f", loading))),
              size = if (k_items > 12) 2.1 else 2.8, colour = "grey15") +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                         midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "loading") +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(row_labels),
                     labels = scales::label_wrap(TEXT_CAP)) +
    labs(title = paste0(block_name, ": ", rotation, " loadings"),
         subtitle = paste0(k_items, " items, ", k, " component",
                           if (k != 1) "s", "; outlined = |loading| >= ",
                           LOAD_MIN),
         x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey15"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5, colour = "grey15", hjust = 1),
          panel.grid = element_blank())

  list(
    block     = block_name,
    thin      = thin,
    rotation  = rotation,
    n_obs     = n_obs,
    eig       = eig,
    var_pc    = var_pc,
    loadings  = loads,
    table     = wide,
    long      = long,
    alphas    = alphas,
    n_members = n_members,
    kmo       = psych::KMO(R),
    bartlett  = psych::cortest.bartlett(R, n = n_obs),
    near_constant = modal_share >= MODAL_MAX,
    modal_share   = modal_share,
    r_scores  = if (k > 1) fit$r.scores else NULL,
    scree     = scree,
    loadings_plot = loadings_plot,
    retention = data.frame(
      Block      = block_name,
      Items      = k_items,
      n          = n_obs,
      `n/item`   = round(n_obs / k_items, 1),
      `Parallel` = if (thin) "-" else as.character(k_pa),
      `Kaiser`   = sum(eig > 1),
      `PC1 var%` = round(var_pc[1], 1),
      Retained   = k,
      check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  )
}


# =============================================================================
# STANDALONE RUN  --  only when this file is being run, not when it is loaded
# =============================================================================
# ------------------------------------------------------------
```

```{=html}
<h1 id="analyses-pilot-phase">Analyses (main study)</h1>

<div class="block-box">
<strong>Why only simple correlations for now?</strong> The end goal is a
psychological <em>network</em> of these attitude items, but network estimation
needs a much larger sample than this soft launch: at small N the regularised
estimators used in the field (e.g.&nbsp;EBICglasso) give <em>unstable</em> edge
structures and poor specificity, so a network fitted now would not be
trustworthy (Burger et&nbsp;al., 2022). The soft launch is therefore for
<strong>refining the instrument</strong>, and the checks below are chosen with
that paper's reporting standards in mind:
<ul>
<li><strong>Redundancy / &ldquo;topological overlap&rdquo; (their Box&nbsp;A,
    Instrument design).</strong> Items from one questionnaire can be nearly
    redundant; a strongly correlated pair produces an artificially strong edge
    and distorts centrality later. Screening within-block correlations now lets
    you spot pairs that may be measuring the same thing and could be
    reworded, merged, or dropped. The threshold below (|r|&nbsp;&gt;&nbsp;0.5)
    is a <em>pragmatic screen</em>, not a rule from the paper &mdash; the paper
    motivates checking redundancy but does not fix a cut-off (formal tests such
    as <code>goldbricker</code> exist for later).</li>
<li><strong>Variable distribution / variance.</strong> Floor- and ceiling
    effects and near-zero variance restrict range and bias edges and centrality.
    The Descriptive-report tab already shows every item's distribution &mdash;
    watch for items where almost everyone picks one option.</li>
<li><strong>Deterministic relations &amp; skip-structures.</strong> Do not later
    put a sum-score in the network together with its component items, and be
    careful with items only shown to some respondents (skip logic); both induce
    artefactual dependencies. Worth checking the item pool for these now.</li>
<li><strong>Measurement level drives the estimator.</strong> These are ordinal
    Likert / 0&ndash;100 slider items, so plan an ordinal-appropriate estimator
    (e.g.&nbsp;polychoric-based EBICglasso, or <code>mgm</code> for mixed types),
    and report it. That is why the screen below uses <em>Spearman</em>
    (rank-based) rather than Pearson correlations.</li>
<li><strong>Plan the accuracy / stability checks.</strong> When N is large
    enough, assess edge-weight accuracy with a bootstrap (<code>bootnet</code>)
    and centrality stability with the case-drop bootstrap (CS-coefficient,
    ideally &ge;&nbsp;0.5). Running these on the soft launch will simply show poor
    stability &mdash; a concrete signal of how much more data you need.</li>
<li><strong>Report everything.</strong> All preprocessing (recoding, collapsing
    categories, missing-data handling), the estimator and its settings, software
    versions and the random seed &mdash; so the eventual network is reproducible.</li>
</ul>
The table(s) below list, per block, the item pairs whose Spearman
correlation exceeds the threshold. The code is intentionally plain base R so you
can read and edit it (change <code>blocks</code>, <code>threshold</code>, or
<code>method</code>).
</div>
```

```{r analysis-correlations, echo=TRUE, results='asis', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.height=6.2, fig.width=9.5}
# ---- Within-block correlation matrices: a pilot redundancy screen -----------
# One matrix per block of items. Spearman correlations (the items are ordinal);
# the colour runs blue (negative) - white (zero) - red (positive), so a strongly
# red off-diagonal cell is a candidate for redundancy: near-duplicate items
# inflate edges and distort centrality once a network is estimated
# (Burger et al., 2022). Pairs at or above `threshold` are outlined in black.

# BLOCK_NAMES and TEXT_CAP come from PCA.R, sourced in the setup chunk, so the
# screen and the per-block PCA below cannot disagree about what a block is or
# how much wording fits on an axis. The COLUMNS differ deliberately: the screen
# reads the raw items (it is looking for duplicated questions, and reversing an
# item does not change which pair is redundant), while the PCA reads the
# reverse-scored copies so that the sign of a loading means something.
# Resolved before the block list so the columns and their labels are subset
# together; emotion_item_labels() returns one label per column of
# emotion_item_columns(), in the same order, so they are paired by name first.
emotion_all     <- emotion_item_columns()
emotion_label   <- setNames(emotion_item_labels(emotion_cols, wording), emotion_all)
emotion_columns <- intersect(emotion_all, names(pilot))

blocks <- setNames(
  list(
    select_items("beliefs",       names(pilot)),
    select_items("gedrag_beleid", names(pilot)),
    subst_cols,
    unname(POLICY_COLUMNS),
    select_items("betrokkenheid", names(pilot)),
    # The emotion question, as topic x emotion binaries ordered topic-major.
    # emotion_item_columns() (R/data.R) builds it from EMOTION_TOPICS and
    # EMOTION_TYPES: 6 topics x 3 emotions.
    #
    # In the POOLED dataset the product is ragged: pilot 1 offered `hoop` and
    # pilot 2 did not, pilot 2 added two topics pilot 1 never asked, so
    # `emo_wod_hoop` is a combination neither instrument put to anyone. Only the
    # columns that exist are kept, and their labels are subset to match.
    emotion_columns
  ),
  c(BLOCK_NAMES, "Emoties")
)
threshold <- 0.5          # flag pairs at or above this |r|
method    <- "spearman"   # ordinal-appropriate; use "pearson" if you prefer

# ---- Three things the emotion block needs and the other five do not ---------
# It is the only block of BINARY items, and that changes what the screen means.
#
# 1. LABELS. `wording` is keyed by the EXPORT columns, which for this question
#    are the topic columns Q28_*; the binaries are derived and have no entry, so
#    every row label would come out NA. They are composed instead.
# 2. THRESHOLD. cor() on 0/1 is the phi coefficient, which is capped by the two
#    base rates - see the note printed with the matrix. At these base rates a
#    large share of the pairs cannot reach 0.5 at all, so screening this block at
#    0.5 would report "no redundancy" when it had only reported "unreachable".
# 3. SEPARATORS. The block is crossed, so the lines between topics are what make
#    a within-topic cluster distinguishable from a within-emotion one.
#
# All three are per-block lookups with a default, so the five existing blocks
# are untouched.
block_labels <- list(
  Emoties = unname(emotion_label[emotion_columns]))
block_threshold <- c(Emoties = 0.3)
# Separators wherever the topic changes, counted from the columns actually
# present rather than assuming every topic contributes the same number - which
# it does not in the pooled dataset.
block_breaks <- list(
  Emoties = local({
    topic <- sub("_(?:boos|bang_bezorgd|hoop|blij|geen_van_deze)$", "",
                 emotion_columns)
    head(cumsum(rle(topic)$lengths), -1)
  }))

for (block_name in names(blocks)) {
  cols <- blocks[[block_name]]
  if (length(cols) < 2) next

  item_matrix <- as.matrix(pilot[cols])
  # items are numbered by their position in the block, which is survey order
  numbers   <- as.character(seq_along(cols))
  full_text <- if (is.null(block_labels[[block_name]]))
    sub("^.*? - ", "", gsub("[\r\n]+", " ", wording[cols])) else
    block_labels[[block_name]]
  block_r   <- if (is.na(block_threshold[block_name]))
    threshold else unname(block_threshold[block_name])
  # The ROW axis carries the item wording itself, so a cell can be read without
  # looking anything up. The columns keep the bare numbers, since the wording
  # cannot be shown twice at a readable size.
  #
  # WRAPPED, not truncated. Cutting the text at a character count is what makes
  # items indistinguishable when several share an opening clause - and the part
  # that identifies an item is often the end of it.
  row_labels <- paste0(numbers, ". ", full_text)
  colnames(item_matrix) <- numbers

  R <- cor(item_matrix, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = method)

  # long format for a tile plot; keep the lower triangle plus the diagonal
  long <- expand.grid(row = numbers, col = numbers, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  long$r <- as.vector(R)
  long <- long[match(long$row, numbers) >= match(long$col, numbers), ]
  # Undefined correlations arise when an item is constant or has no overlapping
  # observations. Show them in the matrix, but never treat them as flagged pairs.
  long$flag <- !is.na(long$r) & abs(long$r) >= block_r & long$row != long$col
  long$row_lab <- factor(row_labels[match(long$row, numbers)], levels = row_labels)
  long$col <- factor(long$col, levels = numbers)

  n_flag <- sum(long$flag, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat("\n\n###", block_name, paste0("(", length(cols), " items, ", n_flag,
      " pair", if (n_flag != 1) "s", " with |r| >= ", block_r, ")"), "\n\n")

  # What a reader has to know before reading THIS matrix, computed from the data
  # rather than asserted: how many of its pairs the usual 0.5 screen could not
  # have flagged whatever the respondents answered.
  if (block_name == "Emoties") {
    rates <- colMeans(item_matrix, na.rm = TRUE)
    ceiling <- outer(rates, rates, phi_max)
    unreachable <- sum(ceiling[upper.tri(ceiling)] < threshold)
    cat("These items are binary, so this is the **phi** coefficient",
        "(on 0/1 columns Spearman, Pearson and phi are the same number).",
        "Phi is bounded by how often the two items are ticked: here the rates",
        "run from", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.2f", min(rates))), "to",
        sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.2f", max(rates))), "and", unreachable, "of the",
        sum(upper.tri(ceiling)), "pairs could not reach |r| =", threshold,
        "whatever the answers had been. This block is therefore screened at",
        paste0(block_r, ","), "and a low cell may mean the two items are",
        "ticked too differently often for phi to be large rather than that they",
        "are unrelated.\n\n")
  }

  plot <- ggplot(long, aes(x = col, y = row_lab, fill = r)) +
      geom_tile(colour = "white") +
      geom_tile(data = long[which(long$flag), ], colour = "black", fill = NA) +
      geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(
        as.character(col) == row, "",
        ifelse(is.na(r), "NA", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.2f", r)))
      )), size = if (length(cols) > 12) 2.1 else 2.8, colour = "grey15") +
      scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                           midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), na.value = "grey75",
                           name = "r") +
      scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(row_labels),
                       labels = scales::label_wrap(TEXT_CAP)) +
      labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
           caption = "Grey cells labelled NA are undefined correlations.") +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey15"),
            axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5, colour = "grey15", hjust = 1,
                                       lineheight = 0.9),
            panel.grid = element_blank())

  # Group separators, for a block whose items are crossed rather than a flat
  # list. The y axis is drawn reversed, so a break after item k sits at k + 0.5
  # counting across but at n - k + 0.5 counting up.
  breaks <- block_breaks[[block_name]]
  if (!is.null(breaks))
    plot <- plot +
      geom_vline(xintercept = breaks + 0.5, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.35) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = length(cols) - breaks + 0.5, colour = "grey40",
                 linewidth = 0.35)
  print(plot)
}
```

### All blocks together

The matrices above only look *within* a block, which is where near-duplicate
wording is most likely. Redundancy can cross blocks too — a belief item may
track a policy slider closely — so the same screen is repeated over every item at
once. Items are prefixed with their block (**B** beliefs, **G** gedrag,
**S** middelengebruik, **P** beleidsvoorkeur, **I** betrokkenheid) and the
numbers match the per-block matrices above, where the full wording is shown.

The emotion items are deliberately **not** in this matrix. They are binary, so
their cells would be phi coefficients sitting beside Spearman ones under a single
flag threshold that does not mean the same thing in each — and, as the note above
that block explains, a threshold most of those pairs cannot reach.

```{r analysis-correlations-all, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.height=9.5, fig.width=9.5}
# ---- One matrix over every item in the survey -------------------------------
# Same method and threshold as the per-block matrices. Only the strongest pairs
# are labelled with their r: at 46 x 46 the numbers are unreadable, and what
# matters here is WHERE the strong blocks of correlation sit, not their exact
# size. Thin white lines separate the blocks.
# one short axis-label prefix per block, in the same order as `blocks` above
block_letter <- c("Beliefs" = "B", "Behaviour" = "G", "Substance use" = "S",
                  "Policy preference" = "P", "Involvement" = "I")

# An EMPTY block is dropped from this matrix. The pooled dataset has no gedrag
# items - pilot 1's four were replaced by three new ones, so none is common to
# both pilots - and `paste0("G", integer(0))` is "G", not character(0), because
# paste0 treats a zero-length argument as "". That stray label made the label
# vector one longer than the matrix, and the failure surfaced as a dimnames
# length error with nothing pointing at the empty block.
block_letter <- block_letter[lengths(blocks[names(block_letter)]) > 0]

all_cols   <- unlist(unname(blocks[names(block_letter)]))
all_labels <- unlist(lapply(names(block_letter), function(b)
  paste0(block_letter[[b]], seq_along(blocks[[b]]))))
stopifnot(length(all_cols) == length(all_labels))

all_matrix <- as.matrix(pilot[all_cols])
colnames(all_matrix) <- all_labels
R_all <- cor(all_matrix, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = method)

long_all <- expand.grid(row = all_labels, col = all_labels, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
long_all$r <- as.vector(R_all)
long_all <- long_all[match(long_all$row, all_labels) >= match(long_all$col, all_labels), ]
long_all$flag <- !is.na(long_all$r) &
  abs(long_all$r) >= threshold & long_all$row != long_all$col
long_all$row <- factor(long_all$row, levels = all_labels)
long_all$col <- factor(long_all$col, levels = all_labels)

# where one block ends and the next begins, for the separator lines
block_ends <- head(cumsum(lengths(blocks[names(block_letter)])), -1)

ggplot(long_all, aes(x = col, y = row, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", size = 0.15) +
  geom_tile(data = long_all[which(long_all$flag), ],
            colour = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = long_all[which(long_all$flag), ],
            aes(label = sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.2f", r))),
            size = 1.9, colour = "grey10") +
  geom_text(data = long_all[which(is.na(long_all$r)), ],
            label = "NA", size = 1.4, colour = "grey15") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = block_ends + 0.5, colour = "grey40", size = 0.35) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = block_ends + 0.5, colour = "grey40", size = 0.35) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), na.value = "grey75",
                       name = "r") +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(all_labels)) +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       caption = "Grey cells labelled NA are undefined correlations.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5,
                                   colour = "grey15"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6, colour = "grey15"),
        panel.grid = element_blank())
```

```{r analysis-correlations-all-flagged, echo=TRUE}
# The cross-block pairs that clear the threshold, listed with their wording so
# the matrix above does not have to be squinted at.
cross <- long_all[which(long_all$flag), ]
# as.character() is essential here: `row` and `col` are factors by this point,
# and sub() on a factor works on its integer codes, not its labels - which
# silently emptied this table when it was written without the conversion.
cross$code_row  <- as.character(cross$row)
cross$code_col  <- as.character(cross$col)
cross$block_row <- sub("[0-9]+$", "", cross$code_row)
cross$block_col <- sub("[0-9]+$", "", cross$code_col)
cross <- cross[cross$block_row != cross$block_col, ]
cross <- cross[order(-abs(cross$r)), ]

if (nrow(cross) == 0) {
  cat("No cross-block pair reaches |r| >=", threshold, "\n")
} else {
  label_of <- function(code) {
    v <- all_cols[match(code, all_labels)]      # axis code -> column name
    paste0(code, ". ", cap_text(sub("^.*? - ", "", gsub("[\r\n]+", " ", wording[[v]])), 55))
  }
  knitr::kable(data.frame(
    item_1 = vapply(cross$code_row, label_of, character(1)),
    item_2 = vapply(cross$code_col, label_of, character(1)),
    r = round(cross$r, 2), row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE),
    row.names = FALSE,
    caption = paste0("Cross-block pairs with |r| >= ", threshold))
}
```


```{r setup-pca, include=FALSE}
library(here)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7, dpi = 110)
```

```{=html}
<h1 id="per-block-pca">Per-block PCA: does each block have a structure?</h1>

<div class="block-box">
<strong>The screen above and this section decompose the same matrix.</strong>
A correlation screen answers &ldquo;which <em>pairs</em> of items are
near-duplicates?&rdquo;. It cannot answer &ldquo;does this block have a
<em>structure</em>?&rdquo; &mdash; a block can contain no pair above
|<em>r</em>|&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.5 and still be two clean dimensions, or be one
dimension with a tail of weakly related items. What follows runs a principal
component analysis on exactly the same Spearman matrix each figure above plots,
so the two read as one argument rather than two analyses.
<br><br>
<strong>These components are estimated within one block at a time.</strong>
The pooled sub-scale solution of the pilot reports ran one analysis over the
belief and behaviour items together. C1 here is not the C1
there, and the two numberings must never be read as interchangeable. This is a
check on whether the blocks are sensible groupings, not a replacement for that
solution.
<br><br>
<strong>Two blocks are deliberately not the same columns as the screen.</strong>
Beliefs and Behaviour use the reverse-scored copies, so that high means
&ldquo;more pro-liberalisation&rdquo; on every item; without that the sign of a
loading would record how an item happened to be worded rather than what
respondents think, and the first component would come out as a wording artefact
instead of a dimension.
<br><br>
<strong>How many components each block gets</strong> is decided by parallel
analysis (Horn, 1965) rather than by eigenvalues over 1, which is known to
over-extract. Blocks shorter than five items are not asked the question at all:
with three or four items there is not enough covariance structure for a second
component to mean anything, and rotation is undefined for a single one.
</div>
```

```{r pca-retention, echo=TRUE}
# PCA.R is sourced in the setup chunk; its RUN_STANDALONE guard means nothing
# ran on import. pca_block() is the same function `Rscript PCA.R` calls, so the
# console script and this tab cannot drift apart.
# BLOCKS_FITTED rather than BLOCKS: a block with fewer than two items has no
# component solution, and in the pooled dataset `Behaviour` has none at all.
pca_results <- lapply(names(BLOCKS_FITTED),
                      function(b) pca_block(BLOCKS_FITTED[[b]], b, pilot))
names(pca_results) <- names(BLOCKS_FITTED)

knitr::kable(
  do.call(rbind, lapply(pca_results, `[[`, "retention")),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = paste("How many components each block supports. 'Parallel' is what",
                  "parallel analysis suggests, 'Kaiser' counts eigenvalues",
                  "over 1 (shown for comparison only - it over-extracts), and",
                  "'Retained' is what was actually fitted."))
```

**Read `n/item` first.** It is the thinnest part of this soft launch: a stable
component solution wants something like 10 respondents per item, and the
`n/item` column shows how far each block is from that. Nothing below is a result about drug
attitudes — it is a check on whether the blocks hang together well enough to be
worth keeping as blocks.

```{r pca-blocks, echo=TRUE, results='asis', fig.height=6.2, fig.width=9.5}
# One section per block: the diagnostics that decide whether the solution is
# readable at all, then the loadings, then the two figures. `results='asis'`
# so the per-block headings become real headings in the sidebar.
for (result in pca_results) {
  k     <- result$retention$Retained
  items <- nrow(result$table)

  cat("\n\n## ", result$block, " (", items, " items, ", k, " component",
      if (k != 1) "s", ")\n\n", sep = "")

  # The caveats that decide how much weight the solution can carry, stated
  # rather than implied.
  notes <- c(
    if (result$thin)
      paste0("**Reduced report.** Fewer than ", MIN_ITEMS_PCA, " items: one ",
             "component, no rotation, no per-component reliability. A block ",
             "this short cannot support a component structure, and its KMO is ",
             "near meaningless."),
    if (result$n_obs / items < 10)
      paste0("**", round(result$n_obs / items, 1), " respondents per item.** ",
             "Treat the solution as provisional."),
    if (result$n_obs < nrow(pilot))
      paste0("The correlation matrix is pairwise over all ", nrow(pilot),
             " respondents; parallel analysis and reliability use the ",
             result$n_obs, " complete cases."),
    if (any(result$near_constant))
      paste0("**Near-constant items:** ",
             paste0("`", result$table$variable[result$near_constant], "` (",
                    round(100 * result$modal_share[result$near_constant]),
                    "% give one answer)", collapse = ", "),
             ". Too little variance to load anywhere; consider dropping them ",
             "before reading the solution."),
    paste0("KMO = ", round(result$kmo$MSA, 2), " (lowest item ",
           names(which.min(result$kmo$MSAi)), " = ",
           round(min(result$kmo$MSAi), 2), ")",
           if (result$kmo$MSA < 0.50) ", below 0.50 and barely factorable",
           "; Bartlett *p* ",
           format.pval(result$bartlett$p.value, eps = .001),
           "; ", round(sum(result$var_pc[seq_len(k)]), 1),
           "% of variance in ", k, " component", if (k != 1) "s",
           " (", result$rotation, " rotation)."),
    if (!result$thin)
      paste0("Reliability: ",
             paste0("C", seq_len(k), " ", result$n_members, " items, ",
                    ifelse(is.na(result$alphas), "too few for alpha",
                           paste0("alpha = ", round(result$alphas, 2))),
                    collapse = "; "), ".")
  )
  cat(paste(notes, collapse = "\n\n"), "\n\n")

  loading_table <- result$table[order(result$table$primary,
                                      -result$table$prim_load), ]
  # left at full length: a kable cell wraps in HTML, so truncating here only
  # loses the end of items that share an opening clause
  print(knitr::kable(
    loading_table[, setdiff(names(loading_table), c("block", "prim_load"))],
    row.names = FALSE,
    caption = paste0(result$block, ": loadings, sorted by component. ",
                     "'primary' is the component an item belongs to, or - if ",
                     "its strongest loading is under ", LOAD_MIN, ".")))
  cat("\n\n")

  print(result$scree)
  print(result$loadings_plot)
}
```
